description: Atomic-braid recipe for deuteron in the canonical operator-valued convention (`canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings(1, 1)`).  Status: SDP-optimum verified for deuteron via PR #608's `r5_full_canonical_knot_solver` (the canonical word lies in the LP-optimum class for the (Z = 1, N = 1) atom under the operator-selection LP).  23 crossings on 6 strands.  Trust profile {axiom: 2, derived: 3, script-cited: 3}.  Canonical companion to the per-atom mass-trace `atomic-braid-recipe-d` SCRIPT_CITED step declared in PR #605's `markov-trace-assembly-deuteron.derivation.json`; that consumer does not yet reference this artifact, so the SCRIPT_CITED step there remains pending until the reference is wired up downstream.  Closure of `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp` (issue #604 GAP-A-1) upgrades all three SCRIPT_CITED steps to LEAN_PROVEN simultaneously, at which point the legacy-disjoint variant can be deleted in favour of this chain.

steps.name: Categorical R-matrix action of B_{6} on V^{⊗6}
steps.operation: By the categorical-action axiom (FirstPrinciple `Cat.Action`), each braid generator `σ_i ∈ B_6` acts on `V^{⊗6}` (V the fundamental quark representation of `U_q(sl_2)`) via the Drinfeld–Jimbo R-matrix at strand `i`.  The action factors through the Hecke algebra `H_6(q)` by the quadratic relation `σ² = h·σ + 1` with `h = q − q⁻¹`.
steps.output_value: σ_i : V^{⊗6} → V^{⊗6} via R-matrix at strand i

steps.name: Quark / nucleon irrep assignment via Schur–Weyl
steps.operation: By Schur–Weyl duality (FirstPrinciple `Schur`), the quark sits in `V`, the fundamental of `U_q(sl_2)`.  A nucleon is a 3-quark composite living in the color-singlet block of `V^{⊗3}`; its braid statistics are governed by `H_3(q)` acting on `V^{⊗3}`.

steps.name: Canonical proton word in B_3 (operator-valued)
steps.operation: Per `mass_at_3A_proper.atom_braid_word_3A(Z=1, N=0)`, the proton's canonical Hecke normal form is the 11-crossing word `[(0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'averaged'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'averaged')]` in the operator-valued convention with averaged crossings `I = σ − (h/2)·1`.  PR #608's SDP solver (`r5_full_canonical_knot_solver`) confirms this word is in the LP-optimum canonical-knot class identified by `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp`.
steps.notes: script: folio-assistant/computations/mass_at_3A_proper.py (`atom_braid_word_3A`) + folio-assistant/computations/canonical_braid_crossings.py (`atom_canonical_crossings(1, 0)`).  Awaits Lean formalisation of the (uud) → canonical-NF map; closes when `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp` (issue #604, GAP-A-1) graduates to a theorem (categorical SDP uniqueness).

steps.name: Canonical neutron word in B_3 (operator-valued)
steps.operation: Per `mass_at_3A_proper.atom_braid_word_3A(Z=0, N=1)`, the neutron's canonical Hecke normal form is the 11-crossing word `[(0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'averaged'), (0, 'averaged'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv')]` in the operator-valued convention.  Differs from the proton by the averaged-vs-σ pattern at strand-1 positions 4–5, encoding the (udd) quark-content signature.  Same SDP-LP-optimum status as the proton via `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp`.
steps.notes: script: folio-assistant/computations/canonical_braid_crossings.py (`atom_canonical_crossings(0, 1)`).  Same closure path as the proton word (step 3): when `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp` becomes a theorem, both step 3 and step 4 rebase to LEAN_PROVEN simultaneously.

steps.name: Inter-nucleon averaged crossing rule
steps.operation: For atoms with `A ≥ 2`, the inter-block crossing between nucleon blocks `k` and `k + 1` sits at the 0-indexed generator `3k − 1` (for `k = 1..A − 1`); it is the averaged operator `I_{3k−1} := σ_{3k−1} − (h/2) · 1`, encoding the `pp`, `pn`, `nn` channel selection of `prop:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition`.  For single-nucleon atoms (A = 1) this step contributes no crossings; for the deuteron (A = 2, pn channel) it contributes one averaged crossing at gen_idx 2.
steps.notes: script: folio-assistant/computations/mass_at_3A_proper.py (`atom_braid_word_3A` inter-block insertion logic).  Paper-cited under `prop:hecke-branching-trace-decomposition`; awaits Lean formalisation of the operator-valued interface — same Lean status as `conj:canonical-knot-id-sdp`'s categorical proof.

steps.name: Disjoint-block embedding B_3 ↪ B_{6}
steps.operation: For an atom with `A = 2` nucleons, the disjoint-strand embedding `B_3 ↪ B_{6}` for the `k`-th nucleon block (`k = 1..2`) is the index shift `σ_i ↦ σ_{i + 3(k - 1)}` extended sign-preservingly to negatives and to the averaged crossings.  Generators are **0-indexed** here to match the `(gen_idx, ctype)` output of `canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings`; so `i, gen_idx ∈ {0, 1}` for the in-block generators of `B_3` and `gen_idx + 3(k-1) ∈ {0, 1, ..., 4}` for the embedded `B_{6}` generators (i.e. σ_g ranges over `g ∈ {0, ..., 4}`).  Standard disjoint-product structure of the braid group: blocks of strands `3(k-1), ..., 3k - 1` are independently braided.

steps.name: Atom assembly rule T_w(deuteron) ∈ B_{6}
steps.operation:
Combine steps 3–6 into the atom assembly:
  T_w(Z = 1, N = 1) := 
    ∏_{k=1}^1 (proton word shifted by block k) ∘
    ∏_{k=Z+1}^{2} (neutron word shifted by block k) ∘
    ∏_{k=1}^{2-1} (inter-nucleon averaged crossing at 0-indexed generator 3k − 1).
Pure algebra: sequence of disjoint-block + interface crossings concatenated in B_{6}.

steps.name: Specialisation: deuteron = (Z = 1, N = 1)
steps.operation: Apply the assembly rule at (Z = 1, N = 1) to obtain the 23-crossing canonical word `[(0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'averaged'), (0, 'sigma'), (0, 'sigma'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'sigma_inv'), (1, 'averaged'), (2, 'averaged'), (3, 'sigma'), (3, 'sigma'), (3, 'sigma'), (3, 'averaged'), (3, 'averaged'), (3, 'sigma'), (3, 'sigma'), (4, 'sigma_inv'), (4, 'sigma_inv'), (4, 'sigma_inv'), (4, 'sigma_inv')]` in B_{6}.  Internal assertion in the builder guards that the assembly reproduces `canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings(1, 1)` bit-for-bit.
